remarks:
ENGLISH LITERATURE - School does not have a specific examination for this and any candidate who wants to take this will have to score extremely highly on the Oxford Placement Tests and English Test for Overseas Students that you already hold. [24 Sep 2012]
 
DT - Candidates does not require to sit a test for this subject. [24 Sep 2012]
 
RS - Candidates will need to score highly enough on the Oxford Placement and our English Test and be strong enough with their English to cope with this as an essay based subject. [24 Sep 2012]
 
MUSIC - We do not have an examination but any candidate wishing to take Music will need to provide us with details of their Musical Achievements and Ability for us to review. [24 Sep 2012]
 
NON-VERBAL REASONING -
The level of the NVR paper is dependant on the candidate’s age as at the date they are taking the tests. If at the date of taking the tests the candidate is aged between 12 and 14 (12 yrs 0 months to 14yrs 11 months) they will need to take booklet F. If their age at the date of taking the tests is 15 or more they take booklet G. Should you have anyone applying for a day place aged 10 to 11 (10yrs 0 months to 11yrs 11 months) they will take booklet E. [25 Sep 2012]
 
All candidates MUST request their current schools to complete and return "Confidential Report" to City of London Freemen's School directly. [25 Sep 2012]

remarks:
On receipt of an application:
•	The application will be acknowledged by our Admissions Secretary and logged onto our database
•	An application pack will be compiled for each student to include: 
o	The completed application form
o	Copies of the student’s latest school reports (over the previous two years)
o	Copy of the student’s passport
o	Any other information that might be helpful (copies of certificates or references for example) 
o	Results of the entry tests

Applications will then be held and assessed alongside all other applications for the same entry date in line with the following time scales:

•	Decisions for September entry will be made on 1st October (11 months prior to the entry date), i.e. applications for entry in September 2016 will be reviewed on 1st October 2015.
•	Decisions for January entry will be made on the 1st October (15 months prior to the entry date), i.e. applications for entry in January 2016 will be reviewed on 1st October 2014.  

Students will then either be offered a place to study in our GCSE or A Level classes, offered a place on the waiting list or their application will be declined.

Should any places remain available after the allocation and acceptance of offers each year; they will be offered to students who are on Concord’s waiting list or those who meet our entry criteria as they apply.

Applications which do not meet our entry criteria will be notified at the time of submission, or as soon as it is apparent that the entry criteria have not been met.

This change of policy has been driven by the increased competition for places at Concord.

remarks:
***Closing date for applications: 1st October 2014
Examination dates: Saturday 1st November @AA
Interviews date: All shortlisted candidates will be interviewed by Dauntsey’s representative in HK on 15&16th November. Successful candidates will be informed by Monday 1st December.

School only consider candidates from Band 1 schools or equivalent,  and also looking for students who show evidence of interests and ability in areas such as music, sport, drama and art.  All candidates must have excellent written and spoken English.

The cost of examinations is HK$1000, payable directly to AA before exam.  This is in addition to the £100 registration fee, payable directly to Dauntsey’s School as part of the Registration process.

Application is made by completing the registration form, recent school report and agent’s summary or CV; and submitting it to the Admissions Office together with the registration fee payable by bank transfer. (School will also accept UKiset tests.)  

All completed applications will be reviewed by the Director of Studies who will then recommend selected applicants for examinations.  (28 Mar , 2014)

remarks:
An initial application should include:
1. an agent overview of the candidate and comments from interview
2. the latest school report
3. ideally, a short essay by the candidate giving information about themselves, their interests, achievements and ambitions

Initial application for 2014 should be received by Monday 14th October (this involves completing the reg form and fee)

Registration must be completed by Monday 28th October 2013 for those wishing to take entrance examinations in November 2013 for entry in September 2014.

Exemptions for examinations are given for EAL if a candidate has a relevant IELTS certificate and for Sixth Form entry if a candidate is taking or has taken recognised public examinations (e.g I/GCSE)

Examinations are held either at Dauntsey’s on 13th November 2013 or by arrangement at an agent’s offices or offices of the British Council (location to be advised for 2014 entry).

***School still consider able candiates outside these dates and will interview in person during the visit of the Head Master and Director of Studies to Hong Kong in mid January 2014.***

Closing date for applications:  	Friday 25th October 
Examination date:  		Sunday 17th November at 10.00 am at the Royal Garden Hotel, Kowloon, Hong Kong.
Successful candidates will be informed by Monday 2nd December.

[2 Oct 2013]
We will now be processing students in three tranches: December, April, and June.

This should work in the following way: the first deadline will be the first Friday of December of the year before entry; those students who have applied before that date will be looked at and processed in the first round.  All applications which have been received by that first Friday will be sifted through and students will have the results of their application within two weeks after cut-off date. Students will then have a week to decide whether to accept an offer if they have been given one. So the main change is that students will only have the result of their applications two weeks after the end of the deadline in whichever time period they have applied (December, April or June). Otherwise, students will be processed in terms of interviews and testing as at present.      

Applications received any time after the first Friday of December (6/12/2013) will be considered in the second round and students will be notified two weeks after that session closes - the session ends the first Friday in March (7/03/2014). Again once the Admissions cut-off date is reached – all the applications that have been received and dealt with are decided upon and the students are duly informed within a two week turn around. Please note that our places will be mainly full by January therefore we strongly advise that you inform your students to submit applications in the first batch. We are very unlikely to still have places left after the second batch. 

The final student intake has to be received by the first Friday in June (6/6/2014) – by which stage most of the individual student applications will have been processed. Given the lateness of these applications once an offer has been made to the student they will need to accept or decline it within a week of receipt.

On receipt of an application:
•	The application will be acknowledged by our Admissions Secretary and logged onto our database
•	An application pack will be compiled for each student to include:

Applications will then be held and assessed alongside all other applications for the same entry date in line with the following time scales:

•	Decisions for September entry will be made on 1st October (11 months prior to the entry date), i.e. applications for entry in September 2016 will be reviewed on 1st October 2015.
•	Decisions for January entry will be made on the 1st October (15 months prior to the entry date), i.e. applications for entry in January 2016 will be reviewed on 1st October 2014.  

Students will then either be offered a place to study in our GCSE or A Level classes, offered a place on the waiting list or their application will be declined.

Should any places remain available after the allocation and acceptance of offers each year; they will be offered to students who are on Concord’s waiting list or those who meet our entry criteria as they apply.

Applications which do not meet our entry criteria will be notified at the time of submission, or as soon as it is apparent that the entry criteria have not been met.

This change of policy has been driven by the increased competition for places at Concord.

remarks:
New online registration process for 16+ entry to Wellington College which we are implementing from this year onwards. 
 
In order to make registering a child for Sixth Form entry at Wellington as easy as possible, the whole process is now to be completed via a few clicks from our website.  There is a link on the 16+ Entry page (http://www.wellingtoncollege.org.uk/2575/admissions/joining-wellington/16-entry) of the Admissions section to our new online registration forms.  This will take you through to two simple forms:
 
1.     16+ Registration form to be completed by parents. This form requires simple personal details, information about pupils’ current schools, and confirmation of how to pay the registration fee.
2.     16+ Personal Statement form to be completed by pupil applicants. This form, amongst other things, requires pupils to:
•         Upload a personal statement written by them (PDF or MSWord, max. 1000 words) detailing their academic and extra-curricular strengths, their reasons for wanting to join Wellington College, and any other information which they feel will strengthen their application
•         Upload their latest set of school reports (we would suggest their reports for the Summer Term 2014)
Once both forms have been completed and the registration fee paid, we will then be able to process the application.

Please note: overseas candidates, for whom English is not their first language, are also required to complete UKiset, an online set of tests as part of the application process. More details can be found at www.ukiset.com.

Applications will then be held and assessed alongside all other applications for the same entry date in line with the following time scales:

•	Decisions for September entry will be made on 1st October (11 months prior to the entry date), i.e. applications for entry in September 2016 will be reviewed on 1st October 2015.
•	Decisions for January entry will be made on the 1st October (15 months prior to the entry date), i.e. applications for entry in January 2016 will be reviewed on 1st October 2014.  

Students will then either be offered a place to study in our GCSE or A Level classes, offered a place on the waiting list or their application will be declined.

Should any places remain available after the allocation and acceptance of offers each year; they will be offered to students who are on Concord’s waiting list or those who meet our entry criteria as they apply.

Applications which do not meet our entry criteria will be notified at the time of submission, or as soon as it is apparent that the entry criteria have not been met.

Applications will then be held and assessed alongside all other applications for the same entry date in line with the following time scales:

•	Decisions for September entry will be made on 1st October (11 months prior to the entry date), i.e. applications for entry in September 2016 will be reviewed on 1st October 2015.

Students will then either be offered a place to study in our GCSE or A Level classes, offered a place on the waiting list or their application will be declined.

Should any places remain available after the allocation and acceptance of offers each year; they will be offered to students who are on Concord’s waiting list or those who meet our entry criteria as they apply.

Applications which do not meet our entry criteria will be notified at the time of submission, or as soon as it is apparent that the entry criteria have not been met.

This change of policy has been driven by the increased competition for places at Concord.

remarks:
On receipt of an application:
•	The application will be acknowledged by our Admissions Secretary and logged onto our database
•	An application pack will be compiled for each student to include: 
o	The completed application form
o	Copies of the student’s latest school reports (over the previous two years)
o	Copy of the student’s passport
o	Any other information that might be helpful (copies of certificates or references for example) 
o	Results of the entry tests

Applications will then be held and assessed alongside all other applications for the same entry date in line with the following time scales:

•	Decisions for September entry will be made on 1st October (11 months prior to the entry date), i.e. applications for entry in September 2016 will be reviewed on 1st October 2015.
•	Decisions for January entry will be made on the 1st October (15 months prior to the entry date), i.e. applications for entry in January 2016 will be reviewed on 1st October 2014.  

Students will then either be offered a place to study in our GCSE or A Level classes, offered a place on the waiting list or their application will be declined.

Should any places remain available after the allocation and acceptance of offers each year; they will be offered to students who are on Concord’s waiting list or those who meet our entry criteria as they apply.

Applications which do not meet our entry criteria will be notified at the time of submission, or as soon as it is apparent that the entry criteria have not been met.

This change of policy has been driven by the increased competition for places at Concord.
